title: Exam review: Module 4 · inflammatory dermatoses
summary: All 30 questions from the Module 4 end-of-module exam, with the recommended UK answer, why the distractors are wrong and links to the matching condition pages. Themes: Blistering mimics, IM (not IV) adrenaline, SJS vs TEN cut-off, pustular psoriasis vs DH, eczema herpeticum.

article.title: About this review
blocks: Revision key for the DermUSW end-of-module exam for Module 4 (Apr 2024): 30 single-best-answer questions. **Saved** is the answer ticked before submission (not a graded course key). **Recommended** is the teaching answer on current UK guidance (NICE / CKS, BNF, BAD, BASHH, Resuscitation Council UK, UKHSA).

head: Q
Topic
Saved
Recommended
Why, and why the distractors are wrong
Read more
rows: Trainee bricklayer, rough hands then vesicles, feet too (leather boots), better on holiday

Wet cement is an irritant (alkaline) **plus chromate allergy** (cement and leather tanning, which explains the boots/feet). Gloves made of leather contain chromate too. No atopic history. Fungal infection doesn't improve on holiday
4-year-old, red swollen itchy cheeks, flexural scratching, red watery eyes, antibacterial soap made it worse
No ideal option. UK management would be **stop the soap → emollient + soap substitute → mild TCS (hydrocortisone 1%) for the face**, stepping to moderate for short periods if needed

The picture is AE (flexures + face) ± irritant soap. "Establish a diagnosis first" is defensible only if the image is atypical (consider ACD, impetiginisation, or eczema herpeticum if punched-out erosions). **Potent TCS on a 4-year-old's face is not UK practice** (NICE CG57). Emollients alone are insufficient for an active flare. Oral antibiotics only if infected (NG190)
Linear vesicles/bullae on exposed limbs after clearing shrubs near woods
Linear streaks where the plant brushed the skin. In the UK, think also of **phytophotodermatitis** (giant hogweed, rue, citrus) and primula. BP doesn't give linear streaks. Zoster is dermatomal
Pruritic wheals with heat, anxiety and exercise
Small 1–3 mm wheals with a flare, triggered by a rise in core temperature. Solar urticaria needs sun. "Chronic idiopathic" ignores the clear trigger
60-year-old, oral ulcers then flaccid bullae; biopsy = PV
**Urgent dermatology referral and start oral prednisolone** (course key)

Untreated PV progresses, and steroids are the bridge. **UK note:** specialists now give **rituximab + prednisolone** first line (BAD 2017). In primary care, start steroids only with on-call dermatology advice. Doxycycline is for BP. Routine referral is too slow
It needs prior sensitisation and is T-cell-mediated, 48–96 h. A corrosive non-specific response is ICD. Type III is immune complex
Atopic woman, deep-seated itchy palmar vesicles for 6 weeks
Pompholyx (dyshidrotic eczema): potent or very potent TCS short-term + emollients. Prednisolone only for severe flares (specialist). Dapsone has no role. Permethrin only if scabies
2-year-old with AE flaring with pollen; which cell drives the clinical features
**Mast cells** (course key for the immediate type I pollen reaction)

IgE-armed mast cells degranulate on allergen exposure. **Note:** eczema itself is driven by **Th2 T cells** (IL-4/13/31), so "T cells" is defensible for an *eczema* flare. Read the stem: "manifestation after exposure to pollen" suggests type I
More than 6 weeks = chronic. Urticarial vasculitis lasts >24 h with bruising. Autoimmune urticaria is a subtype that needs specialist tests
19-year-old, burning prodrome, painful vesicles on the back, 2 days, well
**Oral aciclovir 800 mg five times daily for 7 days**
Shingles <72 h with **moderate–severe pain/rash** meets CKS criteria for antivirals even if young and truncal. Flucloxacillin is for bacterial infection. Don't wait for swabs
Raindrop plaques 2 weeks after a sore throat
Post-streptococcal. PR has a herald patch and collarette. Drug reaction is possible but the morphology fits guttate
Eyelid ACD to new cosmetics; which metal
The commonest UK metal allergen (eyeshadow and mascara pigments, and from fingers). Cobalt and chromate are also possible
Itch and erythema beyond the sutures under an adhesive dressing after C-section
The pattern matches the plaster outline. Infection would centre on the wound
17-year-old, generalised AE flare including face and eyes, only using 1% HC

**Short course of oral steroid with emollient cover** is the likelier course key for an acute *generalised* flare. UK first-line step-up would really be **moderate–potent TCS for the body + TCI or mild TCS for the face/eyelids** (not offered as a single option)

TCIs (NICE TA82) are second line for moderate–severe AE when TCS has failed or isn't tolerated, and they are ideal for **eyelids/face**, so the saved answer is defensible for the face. Ciclosporin and oral retinoids are specialist. Antibiotics only if infected
21-year-old, itchy bumps → small blisters on distal shins and forearms after a Turkey holiday; nitrofurantoin for 3 days; mucosa normal

Exposed distal sites, a holiday, itchy papules turning to blisters, well, normal mucosa. PV is mucosal, flaccid and occurs in an older age group. BP is elderly. Bullous drug eruption is less likely after a 3-day course with an exposed-site distribution
Swollen lips, face and tongue with difficulty breathing
**IM adrenaline 500 micrograms (0.5 ml of 1 mg/ml) into the anterolateral thigh, repeat after 5 min** (Resuscitation Council UK 2021)
**IV adrenaline is for specialists only** (anaesthesia/ICU, titrated) because of arrhythmia risk. Steroids and antihistamines are not first-line in anaphylaxis
Herald patch then collarette ovals after URTI, asymptomatic
Pityriasis rosea is self-limiting over 6–12 weeks. Erythromycin evidence is weak. Use TCS only if itchy. Check syphilis serology if atypical or at risk
Wheals with scratching, <1 h, chef, lansoprazole
Symptomatic dermographism. Lansoprazole is not causal. Oral steroids are not indicated
14-month-old, nocturnal itch, web-space excoriations, feet vesicles, itchy sibling
Infant pattern (palms/soles, vesicles) + an affected household contact. Treat **all contacts on the same day** with permethrin 5% ×2, one week apart
55-year-old, gradual erythroderma with **salmon** patches, **islands of sparing**, follicular hyperkeratosis, thick yellow nails

Salmon-orange colour, *islands of sparing*, follicular papules and orange palmoplantar keratoderma are the hallmarks. GPP gives sheets of sterile **pustules** with fever (an emergency). Eczema herpeticum and PLEVA don't fit
Sharply defined red plaques with scale; Auspitz sign
Auspitz pinpoint bleeding on removing scale. ACD is ill-defined
60-year-old, very itchy coin-shaped oozing scaly patches on extensor limbs; recurs in cold dry climate

**Oozing**, scaly, intensely itchy, extensors, worse with dryness. GA is a non-scaly, non-itchy ring of papules. Tinea is usually single or asymmetric with a scaly advancing edge (scrape it). NL is shin plaques with yellow atrophy (diabetes)
[Eczema / dermatitis](condition:eczema-dermatitis), [Describing skin lesions: the language of dermatology](condition:lesion-language)
45-year-old, sterile yellow-brown pustules on medial insteps of both feet, burning

Sterile pustules that turn brown on palms or soles, strongly linked to **smoking** and to thyroid autoimmunity. DH is on the extensor limbs and buttocks with tiny vesicles, not plantar pustules. Impetigo herpetiformis is GPP in pregnancy
Inflamed DIP/PIP joints, RF-negative, erosions, raised CRP
**Psoriatic arthritis** (stem omits the skin, but this is the best fit)
Seronegative, DIP-predominant, erosive. Screen with PEST and refer to rheumatology early
Atopic boy, papulopustules at the mouth after repeated 1% HC
Papulopustules triggered by the TCS on top of lip-licking/angular fissuring. Stop the steroid. Topical metronidazole/azelaic acid, or oral tetracycline/erythromycin depending on age
[Rosacea (incl. Demodex & steroid rosacea)](condition:rosacea), [Acne mimics: rosacea, perioral & folliculitis](condition:acne-mimics)
Hand/forearm vesicular ACD hours after mehndi (henna)
Natural henna rarely sensitises. PPD is added to darken it, and later hair dye reactions can be severe. Advise lifelong avoidance
Carbamazepine 1 month, flu-like prodrome, flaccid blisters, **40% BSA**, Nikolsky positive, mucosae involved
Detachment **>30% BSA = TEN** (SJS <10%, overlap 10–30%). Stop carbamazepine and send to ED/burns unit. EM is targetoid, acral and HSV-related. SSSS spares the mucosa
73-year-old, urticated plaques → tense blisters, mucosa normal
Elderly, prebullous urticarial phase, tense bullae, no mucosal involvement. EBA scars. LAD forms annular "string of pearls". PV is flaccid with mucosal involvement
Atopic, unvaccinated child, febrile, grouped vesicles and crusted erosions around the eye/cheek

Grouped monomorphic vesicles/punched-out erosions + fever on a background of AE = HSV. **Same-day** aciclovir and assessment, plus **same-day ophthalmology** (periocular). "Secondary infection" (bacterial) misses the emergency. Impetigo has honey crusts without fever
Pits, onycholysis "oil drops", subungual debris, family history of psoriasis
Pitting + salmon patches/oil drops + onycholysis. Fungal infection usually affects toenails first, and here the toenails are spared. Yellow nail syndrome is slow growth with no pits
[Nail signs: psoriatic nails, Beau’s lines & clubbing](condition:nail-signs), [Psoriasis](condition:psoriasis)

article.title: Where the course answer differs from UK practice

list: **M4 Q5 (PV):** the course says "urgent referral and start prednisolone". UK specialists use **rituximab + prednisolone** first line (BAD 2017). In primary care, start steroids only after a specialist discussion.
**M4 Q2 (child's facial eczema):** none of the options matches NICE CG57. Potent TCS on a child's face is not UK practice.

**M4 Q14 (generalised AE flare):** the UK step-up is to a more potent TCS for the body plus TCI or mild TCS for the face. Oral steroid courses are reserved for severe flares, and TCIs are second line (NICE TA82).
**M4 Q8 (pollen and AE):** "mast cells" is a type I framing. Eczematous inflammation is Th2 T-cell driven.
